### 420.Prov. 24'20a(2_37) edited

Jonathan Edwards

Prov. 24.20. For there shall be no Reward to the Evil man. most of those Proverbs of solomon seem to be Inde pendent sentences with little or no Connection one with another but in this Chapter it is Easy to be observe that the wise man Chiefly insists on the same subject throughout . viz the Great advantage & Benefit of vertue & Godliness & the unprofitable & mischief of ways of sin & wickedness

____________________

He once and again in the Chapter advises us not to Envy sinners wicked men as in the first v. be not thou ----------- as much as to say there is no need of Env nothing to be Got by their way wicked n ways that is worth your Envying em for.

___________________________

In various parts of the Chap. he sets forth the Great advantages & Benefits of ways of Godliness in the 3d verse is described the Great Benefit of it Godliness in its tendency to the Prosp prosperity of a Family Through wisd : is an House Builded & by understanding it is Established

______________

in the 4 v. is set forth the Benefit of th vertue to Increase & in its tendency to Riches or a a plentifull Enjoymt of Earthly substances and by Knowl. -------------------- in the 5 . v. another Benefit of it is declared viz that it increases a mans strength it strengthens a man in any Course or affair he undertakes in [^004-note1] the 13. & 14. verse is set forth the Great Benefit of vertue & Godliness in its tendency to the pleasure that appears in the sweetness of it & its tendency to the Pleasure my son Eat thou Honey . in the 16. v. is set forth the Benefit of it in its tendency to a mans safety from Calamity or deliverance from it or to deliver a man out of Calamity when fallen into it . --------------------------------

___________________________________________________

The and s Thus the wise man sets forth the Profitableness & advantages of ways of Godli ness. & then he dont only do this but also Intermingles observations of the unprofitable & pernicious tendency of ways of sin . in the General he shews it tends to misery Calamity & misery 16 v. the wicked falleth into mischief & in the Latter part of the v. of the Text the Candle of the wicked shall be put out. that is however he show may seem to flourish and Prosper a while yet & his prosperity may seem to be like a Candle that shines bright yet it is put out Like a Candle it soon [-] is hid in darkness & there is a sudden End to all his Glory

_________________

& here are some of the particular Evils that are the fruits of ways of sin set forth . as particularly shame & disgrace v. 9. the thought of foolish ness is sin & the scorner is an abomina. unto man & poverty as in the Last v. so [^004-note2] shall thy Poverty come as one that travileth & thy want as an Armed man.

_________________________________

& in the General the wise man observes that not only do ways of wickedness tend to a Great Deal of Calamity & misery but that they tend to No Good & that no benefit accrues by it Hence he once and again in this Chap. advises us not to Envy wicked men as in the 1 v. Be not thou envious against Evil men neither desire to be with them & so in the v. before the text. fret not thy self because of Evil men neither be thou Envious of the wicked.

& then in the words of the text is the Reason Given why we should not Envy . for there shall be no Reward to the Evil man. that is true i. e. they Get nothing by their wickedness they have nothing that is worthy that we should Envy em for by a Reward have as the word is frequently used in ss the wise man seems to Intend any thing to Benefit obtain’d any Booty or profit Good obtaind to pay em for the [--] trouble of wickedness wicked men are servants they are ma at often at a Great deal of trouble to serve him they do a Great deal whereby they serve an hard master & he Get nothing to Pay em for their Pains the wise man in the 14. v. describes that there shall surely be a Reward of magn [^004-note3] the practice of vertue & piety . so the kmow. of wisd be to thy soul when thou hast found it then there shall be a Reward & thy expecta. shall not be cut off if you have beholden your self to ways of Holiness in hopes of obtaining some Great Benefit by it . you shall not be disappointed your expecta. shall not be Cut off but you shall indeed have some as Great Benefit as you expect . but wicked men tho they expect to Get much but here he says there shall be no Reward to the Evil man. tho wicked men expect to Get much by their sinfull Practices They will in the End surely find thems mistaken they will in the end sur find thems. empty [^004-note4] & wholly disappointed Reaping no Good Fruit of their wickedness.

Reasons. 1. sin is against the Giver of all Good & the maker & dispenser of all things if there there Can be no [-] Good obtained but it must be obtained of G. but how Can it be expected that any thing should be obtaind of him by sinning against him. He has made [^004-note14] the world & has the universal whole universe in his hands all things Consist by him and every thing is ordered by him there is nothing ever Comes to pass any other wise than Just as he dispenses & how theref Can it be expected that any thing should be Got by G Going Contrary to the will & Command of this being seeing that he disposes of Every thing how can it be expected that he should dispense things so a ord as that men should Get any thing by displeasing him & dishonouring him.

__________________________

2. sin is contrary to that fixed Course & order of things that the disposer of all things has Established tis contrary to the Great End of all things which is the Glory of G. G. has made all things for hims. Prov. 16. 4. & as that is the End of all things the Course of all things in that way all tends to Promote the Glory of the Creatour this is the Great Good & Last End that all the Revelations & Changes of things are aiming at in their final Issue & Event they are constantly tending to & theref if we do what is contrary to the Honour of G. we shall see Thwart this Established Course of things & if we Go against that the Established Course of things no other Can be expected than that we shall find the [^004-note15] Course of things to be against us wherein we thwart that we must that that will thwart us. if we live to do what is against the Honour of G. & so cant Go against the End of all things we must expect that the Course of things will be so as to dos oppose our End viz our own Happiness what Every man seeks by is his happiness or Good but this men seek by ways of sin but they ne never any obtained their End by it & no wonder for tis therein they thwart Gods End.

### 423. II Chron. 23:16

### 423.II Chron.23'16 (3_37) edited

Jonathan Edwards

No. 20. Fall March 1737. 2. Chron. 23. 16. and Jehoiada made a Covenant between him and between all the People and between the King that they should be the Lords People. Before this that we have account of in the Text it had been for two or three Reigns a far more degenerate time in Judah than Ever before be There had before been Kings in Judah that did Evil in the sight of the L. and parti that wors worshipped the true G. in a wrong manner Burnt incense in high Places in Contrary to Gods Command that they should offer there sacrifices no where else but in the Place that G. should Choosen & on the alt at his House in Jerusalem & they worshipped the True G. by Images . but Jehoram the Grand- -father of the King spoken of i Joash spoken of in the text Brought in the worship of Baal into Judah & set up Baa this false G. in opposition to the True God. which seems to have been occasioned by his marrying Athaliah the daughter of Ahab who sold hi devoted hims. to this Kind of Jeh the worship of this God his having married Jezebel the daughter of Eth baal the King of the Zidonians as Jezebel perverted ahab & Infected Ahab so athaliah ahabs & Jezebels daughter seems to have Infected Jehoram & ahaziah her son her husband & aha her son ahaziah that succceeded him so that they & the People with them had Cast off of the worship of the L. & Gave thems. up to the worship of Baal & after [^007-note1] Ahaziah was dead Athaliah herself having in an unnatural manner slain all the seed Royal Excepting Joash . Reigned & practiced much as her Brother Jezebel had done so that the true G. had been Cast off H & worshipped during the time of her Reign & the two foregoing Reigns. But during this time of degeneracy Idolatry in Juah. her urs ursurpation & Idolatary Reign . Jehoiada the high Priest who seems to have had a servant zeal for the worship of the True G. Kept Joash. hid in the House of the L. he being his the y youngest of ahaziahs sons in the House of the L. Where he was hid by Jehoshabeath his Aunt hid him when he was but an sucking Infant. we have an Account in this Chap. how Jehoiada Contrived when Joash was about seven years old to Introduce him into the Kingd .& set him upon the Throne of Judah. which being accomplished & athaliah slain he did then proceeded to do as we have an account in the Text to the work that he Principally aimed at in all that he had done. which we have an account of in the Text. wherein may be observed. 1. what that is tha was that Jehoiada what that sought to bring to pass in Judah. viz that the People should be the Lords people. they had of Late in a through the ill example & wicked Governmt of their Kin athaliah & hers son & husband that Reigned before hers forsaken the Lord. withdrawn in a Great measure forsaken the L. & with drawn thems. from being his people. [^007-note2] & . devoted thems. to the worship of Baal to be Baals People. Athaliah the Grand Cause of this apostacy & Idolatry now being dead now slain & Joash that he hims. had Educated long set upon the Throne he now set hims. to bring it about that they might be Cast off other n Gods & Return to the L. that was their of Light the the God that brought em up out of Egypt & to him & distinguished em from other nations to be a Peculiar People to hims. & to to be his People . 2. we may Obs. the way in which he no sought to have this done viz. by a Covenant made & Established to that End. then he would not have their Returning to the L. to be his people to be to be a thing but perfunctorily done. but as a matter of the Greatest seriousness he would have & solemnity & what was done upon measure Consideration & with full Resolution & he would have this Resolution declared & manifested in a Covenant that should be Established that it might be a Matter full that they should fully & explicitly declare & most firmly oblige thems. to. 3 obs. - who were the parties Covenanting or when the Covenant was made between & in the fi & it was in the first place a Covent made between G. & the people - they bound thems. to G.& in Cov. as tis expressed in 2 Kigs [^007-note3] 11. 17. v. And Jehoiada made a Cov. between the L. & the King & the People that they should be the Lords People. . but not only did they in this Cov. bind thems. to G. but also one also the different orders & Ranks of Persons among them bind bound thems. in it one to another tis fi there thus there was a Covenant between the ecclesiastical Authority & the People to this End tis said of Jehoiada the high Priest made a Covenant between him & the People that they would be the Lords People is a they bound thems. by promise one to another that they would Each in their places do their part one towards another that they might be the Lords People. & & it was also made between the Civil Authority & the People or as tis expressed between the King & the People & they bind th firmly bind thems. one to another. also . G. as a G. sitting in a mercy seat & being Ready to be Reconciled to them & to be their God & teaches them the way wherein they may come to Enjoy this Great Priviledge th & they have Gods Gracious offers of Cov. mercy & his Calls & Invitations to Come & partake of the blessings of his Cov.. 2. Her They are a people that he leads in his Provi dence to Enter into Cov. with him. he not only Gives them Light by sending the to them inhis written & preached word wherein his Cov. is Revealed but they are Led visibly at Least to take hold on that Covenant & to Lay thems. under the bonds of it & so to become a professing People of G. & so are brought into a Covenant state this is a Great mercy of G. to any People when he thus brings em into a visible un Covenant union with him. Thes Tho these Proverbs of Solomon are ordinarily unconnected sentences yet there seems here to be a Connection in this verse with both the foregoing & following verse In Each of them there is a Comparison made between the Righteous & the wicked They that are Called tho wicked in the text & following verse is in the foregoing verse Called the fool. & he that is Called the Righ is there Called a man of understanding. in that preceeding verse the wise man observes that Common very Commonly it is a sport to a fool or a wicked man to do mischief or to Commit wickedness . i.e. he does is so stupid & senseless that he does it boldly & without fear he makes Light of it and does it in [---] makes a meer Laughs & sport of it but ano that a man of understanding hath wisdom i.e. a Rig truly wise or Godly man has more Consideration he Considers the dredfull nature & Consequence of wickedness & so is far from making sport of it but dreads it and avoids it & there .

### 437. Cant. 5:3-6

### 437.Cant.5'3-6 (7_37) edited

Jonathan Edwards

July 1737. Cant 5 3 4 5 6 I have put off my coat how shall I put it on I have washed my feet how shall I defile them The spouse of X here gives an account of what passd with respect to her on occasion of a special call that she had from her beloved. we have an account of the call in the foregoing verse where she begins with giving an account of the frame she was in when this call m was made I sleep but my heart waketh the t i. e the tho her heart was awaked tho she had a principle of within her of true Religion that in it self was lively a lively vigorous active principle a principle that of Grace that was forward to duty. yet she by the reason of the prevelency of the canal part was in a dull & sleepy frame indizpo indolent & indisposed to duty.. The expression I sleep but my heart waketh is seems to be of the same import with that which X uses with Respect to his discip. when he saw them in a very dull time Math 2641. what The sp. is willing but the flesh is weak. & then the spouse gives an account how that while she was in this frame X ask her X her beloved & called her it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh [^019-note1] X calls her to arise & open to him to let him in that was the duty he call required of her & the end was that he might come in & he enjoy her company & she his that they might sweetly converse together . He calls her in a very winning manner, with endeer the most endearing expressions & appellations Open to me says he my Love my dove my undefiled. & he calls knocks & calls in a most importunate manner my head says he is filled with the dew sh his s thus knocking at the door of his beloved is represented as being in the night X sought when she was a X sought entertainmt of her and shelter from the dew dews & cold damps of the night In the Text we have an account of what followed with Respect to the spouse who is thus called & at whose door X thus knocks . In which may be observed several things 1. she is slow in answering his call & do opening the door to him as he requested . she did not do as might have been well expected arise & open to him immediately receiving him with the greatest Alacrity & Joy but she is dull about & delays & excuses her self. 2 for want what reason she is thus backward to [^019-note2] hearken to Xs call. viz. that her lothness to deny her self a little to deny her self I have put off my coat how shall I put it on I have washed my feet how shall I defile them . she was in a dull sleepy frame it was was contrary to her to rise out of her bed & put swe drouse & shake off sweet sleep & therefore she finds out excuses she makes an excuse of that that she shall defile her feet if she rises & lets him in. 3. we may observe what how at leng after her delays & excuses she was made willing to comply with Xs call the request of her beloved . he put in his hand & her bowels. X was pleased. when she . when her beloved had called & told her how his head in vain . he further manifested his desire of be entrance by putting in his hand her seeing this moved her she says her bowels were moved for him . it wroght on her affections & made her sensible of her own ingratitude in resisting to being so backward to open to him it roused & made her delay no longer. This seems to be signified by it viz that when the spark of X was not prevaild upon by X’s outw. call the call of his word he then quickend her by his own im mediate hand by drawing forth her heart by the motions of his sp. & therby did as it were put in his hand through the door of her heart and the his voice did not much move her yet [^019-note3] his own hand the voice of X signifies the ex the voice of the beloved probably signifies the ex ternal call of X but the hand of X signifies [his] inward efficacy. tho Xs voice did not move her yet his hand prevail’d . while X called to her she only heard him First upon this but when he put in his hand then she saw something of him she saw his hand Tho having X only only wont prevail on the heart yet when the soul comes to see them something of X that will di have effect. 4. upon this she rises to open to X. G I rose to open to my beloved then after Xs hand had been put in she was willing to obey his hand commands so that she did not utterly R we may observe that she did not utterly refuse to comply with Xs call. The manner of saints & un believers is diff. in this Respect . a natural man utterly Refuses to open to X tho X continues calling from year to time to time . & on the other hand a saint may set at first be backward & shew through a lothness to deny Hims & thereby Greatly sin & but yet they are commonly wont when they have considered the matter at length to comply & yield to their duty they u tis not their man ner absolutely to refuse obedience to [ ] commands of X but will do t at Length [^019-note4] The spouse says of her self that her hands dropped i.e sweet she opend the door to with [shewing] of sweet affection to X. . her heart [began to] be moved from when she first saw him put in his hand through the hole of the door. but after that her affec gracious affection to him pu & desires after him prevailed more & more & no & when she opend the door she did it willingly as with sweet desires after X . 5 we may observe how she was disappointed when she came to open the door But my beloved had . she opend with earnest expectation of meeting her beloved there at the door her heart seemd ready to embrace her hands were perfumd w as it were with sweet smelling myrhmyrrhe ready to be to prepare them to take hold of him & embrace him as soon as ever the door was open . her heart was full of eager desires & expectations of the happy meeting she should there have with him but behold when she had opend the door he was not there but had withdrawn hims. she if she had arose & opend at fir to him when he first calld she ma might have met with him then . but as she says her soul failed when he spake i. e when he first calld her heart faild her she did not find it in her heart then to arise & open to him . [^019-note5] & now she suffers for it now she is risen he is not to be & has opend he is not there. & she says she sought him. Her backward ness to deny herself in her sleepy sluggish frame when he first calld her lost her the benefit of sweet communion with her beloved & not only so but cost her a great of deal of difficulty . for after this she say when she went out about the city to try to find him the watchmen that went & she was sick of love. i. e she was sick & had her heart sunk with her disappointmt of that opportunity of communion with him that she m had met with and so earnestly desired . X hath a [sizeable] an exceeding transcendent Love to his saints he loved them from all Et. his delights were with them before the foundation of the Θ as he says Prov. 8 31 he delighted in them as they existed in his foreknowledge . X certainly then he will not be backward to have communion [^019-note7] with them when they come into being and are after they are savingly brought home to hims. & have his image put upon their souls X loves the saints with a love of complacence he rejoices over them he delights in those holy graces & & those lovely ornaments that he has put upon them his heart is as it were ravished with the sp. beauty that he has given them & he is delighted in their love to him as in the 9. & 10 v of the Chap proceeding the text Thou hast Ravished he manifests his delight to the The souls of the saints are the spouse of J. Song. such is delight in th her that he compares her to the lily among thorns & to a garden enclosed a a fountain of Gardens a well of living w. & streams from Lebanon. Xs love to his saints far exceeds theirs to him love to him . he loved them first & his love is the foundation & th as it were the fountain of theirs His love to them is such that it made him willing willing to die for them & shall not he that was ready to shed his blood & to suffer the cruel & accursd death of the cross for them he also ready to grant them communion with Him yea he died for that end that to make way that they might have communion with him & since he so readily did that surely he will be ready when it is done to attain his own end in it. [^019-note9] X never manifests any backwardness to hold communion with his people but is ever more ready for it & never acts as one that delights in it when they are ready for it he never is backward on his part Prop II . There is nothing required of the saints to make em worthy of communion w such a priviledge nothing by which they can merit it. X stands ready to grant it to them without . he doesn’t need any money or price of theirs to purchase but yet X deals with the saints as reasonable creatures and as capable of actin active creatures & i as tis a mercy to them that he does . and therefore tis expected that they should not be wholly idle & meerly passive in this matter but that they should be actively concernd in what appertains to their coming to this great priviledge of communion with hims. tis an honour that X puts upon them that he orders b it that it should be so that there should be an. intercourse maintaind between him & them so maintaind that they shoud not only not only receive from him but act wherein they should be acti ve & indeed need not it belongs to the notions of communion & converse of two active beings that they should be mutually active . That I may see the Good of thy chosen that I may rejoice in the gladness of thy nation That I may glory with thine inheritance The Main scope of this Psalm seems to be with praisi to Rehearse over Gods wonderfull the wonderfull dispen sations of Gods provid. towards the Chh. of Israel of old in Egypt & in the wilderness & in the Land of canaan & in the name of the Chh. to confess & to Confess the mani fold sins of that people to G. under such great fold sins & instances of great ingratitude in that people from time to time under such wonderfull man appearances of Provid for them. The Psalm consists of three parts First there is the introduc tion to this Rehearsal in the 5 first verses the Introduction to this rehearsal which in in which the forme Psalm is mainly taken up Secondly there is the rehearsal it self from the 6. v. to the 46. in wherein we find a rehearsal of Gods great mercifull dealings with Israel and a particular b account of their provocations intermixed. Thirdly there is the conclusion in the two last verses consisting of a prayer for mercy to [ ] this chh. of Israel & a doxology. or a callng on the chh of Israel to praise him. Our Text is part of the first of these viz the in troduction which consists as the conclusion do of three parts 1 a doxology. in the two [^022-note2] first verses. [ ] The Psalmist having his mind 2. an Instruction 3. full of what he is about to Rehea declare & particularly to Rehearse viz Gods mighty acts & his continual mercy manifest to the Chh. of Israel from time to time calls on Gods people breaks out into praises to G. & calls on others to praise him declaring the sense he had of the m perpetuity of Gods mercy to his chh. & the unspeakeableness of his mighty acts great works towds them. 2 Here is an instruction. blessed This the Psalmist learnt from the consideration of Gods deal past dealings with Isr. that he [ ]is about to Rehearse [ ] how he had from time to time manifested hims. in terrible displeasure towards those that were hypocritical in their pretences & did not keep Judgmt & were not constant in doing right. & his great distinguish to those in Israel that did wholly follow the L. 3. We have an ardent petition of the Psalmist in the text & foregoing v. in the great that he might have a share in the great blessings of Gods true Israel those th last mentioned that were not hypocritical but did keep judgmt & this he is Led led to by the considerations [^022-note3] of the exceeding Glo. acts of mercy that G. had from age to age exercised towards Israel which was for the Elects Gods Invisible chh. the chh. of the Elect or Gods chosen as they are here called were containd in that nation & it was all out of Respect to them that G. wrought much mighty acts & therefor the Psalmist being about to declare these things he Introduces his rehearsal with the a Request that he may share with that happy people an he expresses it in these two verses. Concerning this portion in General I would observe two things request of the Psalmists to be a sharer with Gods People in their blessedness . ### 446. Prov. 24:20(b)

### 446.Prov 24'20 (10_37) edited

Jonathan Edwards

Octob. 1737. Prov. 24.20. The Candle of the wicked Shall be put out . I have formerly spoken. In the 13. & three following verses the wise man had been setting forth the profitableness of ways of wisd. & the happiness of the Godly.

in the 13. & 14. verses is declared the pleasantness of these ways & how that tis well worth while to be found in the practice of Godliness for the sake of the pleasantness of them as much as to eat honey for the sake of its Sweetness to the taste & that the pleasure of Relig. is a good Reward for it. my son & in the 15. & 16. vss is set forth the safety of the Godly in Gods protection, so that h he shall it is in vain for any of their enemies to Lay wait for them & seek their destruction Lay not wait the wise man having thus described the [ ] happiness of ways of holiness he in the words then proceeds in the words that follow to declare the misery of way the wicked unprofitableness & misery of the ways of sin & misery of the wicked in that the wicked shall fall into mis chief i.e they shall ut be utterly destroyed i.e they shall not fall as the Godly do & rise again but they shall fall into utter destruc- [^025-note1] tion & ruin ? then warns us against often re joicing at their calamities or fretting at their prosperity 17 & 18. verses or fretting at their prosperity. & in the text this Case ment we have two Reasons given why we should not fret at the prosperity of wicked men. viz. 1. That they shall never get any thing [ ] by ways of sin. there shall be no Reward to the evil men so that they are not to be envied on the account of any gains they make 2. That [ ] that good prosperity or Good that they seem to enjoy is of very short continuance the candle of the wicked shall be put out. we often find such [ ] expressions used concerning wicked men in SS. as Job. 18.5.6. Yea the light of the wicked shall be put out and the spark of his fire shall not shine the light shall be dark in his tabernacle and his candle shall be put out with him & Chap 21.18 17. How oft is the candle of the wicked put out and how oft cometh their destruction upon them G. distributeth sorrows in his Anger. & so in This book of Prov. 13.9. The light of the righ. rejoiceth but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out. Light is a in SS. is put fo very often put for comfort or prosperity & all indeed [ ] all [^025-note2] good or appearance of Good. & so it seems to be intended in this place both as seems to be manifest from the relation of the words to the foregoing words there shall be no Reward to the evil man. there tis shown how he has no real Good for to Reward him for the service of sin that he does . & her here that in the latter part of the v. that all that seeming Good or appearance of Good that he has shall soon come to an end & also by its relation t the foregoing v. where we are warned not to envy the wicked & the Reason is given for it here viz. that his candle shall be put out now what are more envied for so But for some appearance of Good or prosperity or Good or appearance of G. but here he tells us th shews how they are not to be envied because all that where in they seem to prosper & to have good shall utterly cease be put out The words expression is figurative but exceeding signif comprehensive & seems to signify more than can well be expressed in a few words the other I can otherwise express in a few words & therefore I shall not raise a Doctrine in any other words But shall insist on the words of the text & shew how shall first shew how this Candle of the wicked shall [^025-note3] be put out & shall in many things how this is secondly give the reasons of the doc [ ] fulfilled or wherein the candle of the Wicked is put out 2. It was the custom among them to have their weddings in the night. & the male guests they gathered together at the groom bridg [^026-note3] bridegrooms house to attend on him. but the young women & virgins that were invited they gathered together at the brides house & it was customary wh for a numb of those young women or virgins when they expected the bridegroom to go forth to meet him & because it was in the night it was the custom for every one to take a light in their hands & go forth with their Lamps to meet the bridegroom & so to attend him back & Light the way to the brides house where the marriage was to be attended.
